RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

An all-female panel alone is not evidence of unlawful discrimination. In modern newsrooms, public broadcasters often prioritize digital media transformation over traditional tenure, providing a clear, legitimate rationale for the appointment. Raising the panel's gender directly without concrete evidence will likely appear defensive, damaging your professional standing and relationships.

Instead, follow up politely on your pending feedback request. Focus your inquiries on objective scoring: how the selection criteria were weighted, how your interview was evaluated, and where your qualifications fell short. Only raise the panel's makeup if the broadcaster has an explicit, written policy requiring gender-balanced interview panels, and frame it strictly as a procedural question rather than an allegation of bias.
